answer: SIBAL Cloth was burned in Moon-base air at 31.0 mol % oxygen and 54.1 kPa [data:saffire:table1]. Two-Sided PMMA was burned in Moon-base air at 30.3 mol % oxygen and 54.6 kPa [data:saffire:table1]. Both tests used 20 cm/s concurrent air flow [data:saffire:table1]. No other solid materials in these sources were burned in Moon-base air at these conditions [limits:headline].

chunks.text: The intermediate oxygen concentration used on the Moon will likely be 30% or greater, with a corresponding pressure of 10.2 psi or less. Compared to Earth’s atmosphere, that’s more than a 40% increase in the oxygen concentration making materials much more flammable.

chunks.source: Saffire ICES-2024-365, Table 1, p.3 (rows restated one per test; values checked against the PDF)
chunks.text: Saffire IV-1 (Saffire IV (Cygnus)): SIBAL Cloth, ambient pressure 100.0 kPa, oxygen 22.0 mol %, air flow 20 cm/s concurrent. Saffire V-2 (Saffire V (Cygnus)): Cotton Jersey, ambient pressure 70.7 kPa, oxygen 26.2 mol %, air flow 20 cm/s concurrent. Saffire VI-2 (Saffire VI (Cygnus)): SIBAL Cloth, ambient pressure 54.1 kPa, oxygen 31.0 mol %, air flow 20 cm/s concurrent, in Moon-base air. Saffire VI-3 (Saffire VI (Cygnus)): Two-Sided PMMA, ambient pressure 54.6 kPa, oxygen 30.3 mol %, air flow 20 cm/s concurrent, in Moon-base air. Saffire VI-4 (Saffire VI (Cygnus)): One-Sided PMMA, ambient pressure 55.2 kPa, oxygen 28.8 mol %, air flow 20 cm/s concurrent.

Of the solid-material space fire tests in our sources, only 2 burned in Moon-base air (Saffire VI-2, SIBAL Cloth, 31.0 mol % at 54.1 kPa, 20.0 cm/s; Saffire VI-3, Two-Sided PMMA, 30.3 mol % at 54.6 kPa, 20.0 cm/s), none in partial gravity. Moon-base air means at least 30% O2 at 10.2 psi (70.33 kPa) or less, from the challenge page.

chunks.source: Flame Frontier Known Limits: Space Apps challenge page
chunks.text: Space Apps challenge page gives: Mission context: spacesuit 100% O2 at 4.3 psi; Moon base / rovers at 30%+ O2 and 10.2 psi or less; no partial-gravity combustion data in PSI. It does not give: ACME CFI-G gas-flame tests reached higher O2: "an oxygen-nitrogen mixture of up to 85% oxygen flowed from the spherical burner creating an inside-out flame" (sec. 1). That is the burner's oxidizer stream, not a chamber atmosphere, and not solid materials. Kept off the charts. No lower pressure bound for the Moon-base zone, so the zone is drawn down to 0 kPa.

chunks.source: Flame Frontier habitat gap report: Pressurized rover
chunks.text: Pressurized rover target: ≥30% O2 at ≤70.3 kPa, partial gravity. 2 solid-material tests in this window. Inside ≥30% O2 at ≤70.3 kPa, solids were burned at 20 cm/s airflow only; no solid test in this window at any other flow. Flow is not an axis on Panel 1: every point in the highlighted box shares that flow. Only 2 solid materials burned in ≥30% O2 at ≤70.3 kPa: SIBAL Cloth; Two-Sided PMMA. No flammability boundary (where a solid stops burning) was measured in ≥30% O2 at ≤70.3 kPa. The only one in our data, BASS-II eq. 6.1 for PMMA rods, was measured at 101.3 kPa. No combustion test at partial gravity: every point on both panels is from microgravity. Challenge page: "there is currently no partial-gravity combustion data available in PSI". 2 solid-material tests had O2 and pressure in ≥30% O2 at ≤70.3 kPa: Saffire VI-2, Saffire VI-3. Non-solid tests in ≥30% O2 at ≤70.3 kPa: 20 CFI-G gas flames, 0 FLEX liquid droplets. They do not close a solid-material gap.

question: Which solid materials have been burned in Moon-base air, at 30% oxygen or more and 10.2 psi or less?
